I was on the fence about getting this game originally. Seeing that it was a "speedrun" game normally means it's just a short game that you could replay over and over, BUT to my surprise it's actually decently long for a speedrunning game. Dialog can be a little cringe at times, but a lot anime style games can be like that sometimes. Currently I'm 15.4 hours in which has gotten me to the end of chapter 7 out of 12. During that I spent time on each level collecting the gift and getting at least below the top 500 in all except 1 or 2 level I wasn't fond of. Music, atmosphere, level design, weapon use/discard abilities, they really did a good job. I haven't finished the game yet, but from what I've seen so far, I completely understand why this game has a 98% positive rating.
you spend WAY more time waiting for slow animations or skipping through cringe dialogue than you do playing the game

Heck of a shooter. I'm impressed not just by the levels, weapons and traversal mechanics but how the game pushes you towards improving your times. The goal times are one thing, but the insight system that increases every time you finish a run and lets you see things like ghosts for shortcuts made getting every diamond rank challenging without being overwhelming.

Loved the aesthetics, I think the lower poly environments manage to both help with readability and also include some really striking art. It just felt nice to let the bumping music wash over me as I kept doing run after run. I ended up enjoying the characters and plot (they really knocked it out of the park with the performances), and even if you don't click with them you can just fast forward through.

An excellent parkour/shooting game where you dash and shoot through demons as quick as possible

The greatest quality of the game comes from the arrangement of colours and elements, making it simple enough to track what to do without feeling overwhelmed by the fast pace of the run. You are then able to produce insane tricks and movements without even realising it.

On top of psychedelic soundtracks and challenges to beat the clock by discovering new shortcuts every level, you're in for a very entertaining and rewarding experience

very good game, would recommend for anyone who likes fast-paced shooters or speedrunning

Neon White is an engaging experience that tests a player's reflexes and creativity.

The main objective for most of the levels is to defeat all of the enemies and to reach the goal as fast as you can. Your weapons in games are cards that can either be used as a gun or as a movement ability (e.g. you can use the yellow card as a pistol or as a double jump). The level design always provides a clear route for players to navigate when first going through levels, but are open enough to allow players to experiment and find faster routes. The biggest complement I can give this game is that it gives a strong sense of flow, and that it's easy to enter a flow state. The creative process of finding faster routes and the ease of entering a flow state while executing these routes makes Neon White one of the strongest games to come out in 2022.

I highly recommend Neon White!

Gameplay wise this game is fantastic, addictive and very fast paced. It really makes you feel accomplished after you earn a medal at the end of a level.
It has very nice ways of unlocking and getting tips depending on how quick you completed a map, and some nice end game unlockables too.
With that said, the story and characters were not my favorite part of the game. Thankfully you can fast forward through the cringe inducing performances and dialogue, but you can't entirely skip them.
I'll admit the story might be for a lot of people, but particularly for me I'm grateful I could run through it.
If you're into FPS with a bit of strategy and very fast paced decision making this is the best you can get. If you're into weird anime fantasies and UwU dialogue this might also be for you (?)

Didn't want to proceed to level 2 for a good 20 minutes - that feeling of getting just a few milliseconds off your time just hits different. Sweet satisfaction.

Absolutely love the way this game plays, and though I don't care as much for the visual novel side of things, finding gifts in each level and the side quests that come from interacting with the characters are worth it - plus there's the option to fast track all dialogue so you can dive right back in to clearing levels.

Enjoying the game as of now. Gameplay carries the experience, but it's still a fun ride.

I'm the completionist kind of gamer, yet throughout the years I've noticed I've been less and less interested in putting in all the effort required. Neon White, however, is one of the few games where I am replaying levels even before I completed the story.

Neon White really knows how to create a positive feedback loop, making me really WANT to try the level "just one more time" to get a better time. It actively rewards you for getting a better time even when you're not close to perfect yet. And when you do get close to perfect, it shows you a faster route you can take, to make the level yet again slightly different.

The storywriting and characters, well, it depends. For me, I love them, but I completely understand others will hate them. If "MySpace emo teen who thinks puppies and gore are equally cute" is the kind of cringe you'll hate instead of love, well, you probably will hate these characters. For me personally, I love them, and the story isn't the main game anyway.

For me, this is a great buy, way better than other "speedrunning" games I tried. Do note that half the point of the game is replaying levels to get a better score and without replaying you may rush through the story at an uncomfortable speed, so if you hate replaying levels on principle this may not be your game. Otherwise, it's a solid "parkour" platforming game with solid style and mechanics.
For a 22 dollar game I think this went above and beyond the price. Game is super addicting, story is intriguing, and there's hours of content. Just buy the game trust.
Perfectly encapsulates the base features of a platformer and shooter. The gameplay is smooth and provides great replay value. Excellent soundtrack.
Some of the best gameplay humanity has ever made. Runs on a potato. Highly recommend.

Neon White mixes tight FPS platforming with Trials-esque speedrunning to create a stylish and wildly thrilling experience.

Gameplay is incredibly smooth, there's a sizable amount of content, and the creative level design on display here rivals some of the biggest names in platforming. A one-of-a-kind soundtrack is the cherry on top, perfectly tying together the game's aesthetics. Characters and story unfortunately don't meet the same standards, but they represent a pretty minor sticking point in an otherwise outstanding experience.

I can't recommend this game enough. It might end up being my biggest surprise of 2022. I'm crossing my fingers hard for some DLC.

---

Some suggestions for the developers:

A setting to disable shortcut hints would be appreciated. I had a few "aha!" moments ruined that could have been more fun to discover on my own.

Engaging with the social system between missions can really kill the pace of the game. An option to give multiple gifts at a time might help keep things moving.
press F whenever someone tries to speak, and Neon White becomes an incredibly fun and engaging speed game

I never thought I would have loved a game where the focus was speed running but Neon White proved that wrong. While speed running levels is what the game is based upon there is also an entertaining story from start to finish and gifts to find in most every level. The downtime you have in between story segments is also great as it delivers extra challenges in the form of side quests you can do for the main cast. Greatly enjoyed my time playing Neon White.

The only speed running game that has actively made me interested in improving my times past getting the best medal. The smoothest, most free flowing game when you pull off the combo you’ve been practising for. Its level design is so intuitive that almost anyone can figure out the shortcuts for themselves on a first run. Amazing from start to finish and I even love the dialogue, characters and story. They’re extremely endearing to me.

Yeah this game is pretty incredible. Reminds me a bit of Ultrakill gameplay wise, as it can get extremely fast pace and is 100% for weirdos, but what makes this game so special is the Soul Card system, the speedrunning system (includes the medals ofc), and Level Design, all of which are executed incredibly well. Even if the story is a bit slow at times, it is also pretty good, especially in the memories where you can really see the emotion that drives the characters we see throughout the game. Simply put, this game is well worth it's price, and is an absolute blast to play.

Oh, how fun it is to beat your friends' top times and take things waaaay too seriously.
But honestly, Neon White is a blast. Might be the first game in a good while with gameplay so good, that you can ignore the bad writing and still think really highly of the game. For a crew that allegedly used to be high-profile assassins before the afterlife, they're written like all of them were just chronically online League of Legends players.
Still, it was a really great experience. Especially the last chapters.

Neon White's gameplay is something that I really enjoy, and I've loved playing it thus far, as well as the fact that I love the soundtrack. Unfortunately, the majority of the writing and character dialogue is terrible, and the characters are very two-dimensional, which is unfortunate because of the fact that the voice actors are all pretty okay and could've been directed to actually do something a lot better than what they were given. Also the fact that the Other neons seem to be written to be either really annoying compared to White or really horny towards White (or White is horny for them), it just seems a little too anime tropey for my taste. It also sucks because the world building doesn't seem to be bad, but again a game that's heavily story driven with a terrible script leads to a mid game at best. I saw another reviewer say that if you like anime you should be fine with the dialogue, I like anime and its still unbearable. I wish I could "kinda" recommend this game, because it's not like I don't recommend it because again, I like the game play, but there are too many issues to add to it's Overwhelmingly Positive review score it has on steam.

TL;DR: Gameplay, soundtrack, and world building concept good, script and characters suck.

The visual novel parts are a bit laid back which kinda fits with its gameplay. There's definitely some references and meme quotes here and there that gave me a bit of a chuckle.

A surprisingly addictive speed running game that pushes the player to the limit to find as many shortcuts as possible to even shave off a few nanoseconds.

I found myself losing my mind countless times trying to complete hell rushes as well as trying to beat me best time on a certain level by a few nano seconds. The inclusion of developer times pushes players to the max to hunt for faster times and it gets so addictive that you try to get as low as possible to beat other players times globally. 

The soul card system alongside having an objective of defeating all enemies before ending a level works seamlessly and is fluid and satisfying with every jump, gunshot and bounce. This game is an ADHD'ers dream game. Followed by Machine Girl who did the OST for this game who are an amazing artist with electronic punk. Although their style is toned down in this game, you can tell its them and I absolutely love this soundtrack. It might very well be a top OST for me.

I had a blast playing this game and I urge anyone who wants to look into a speed run style game to give this a try even if you think you are bad. I have no experience in them yet here I am 100% completing it and enjoyed every last moment of it.

In the realm of fast-paced, adrenaline-fueled action games, Neon White stands out as a celestial masterpiece, offering a unique blend of angelic speedrunning and gunplay that will leave you breathless and eager for more.

The gameplay is a masterclass in fluid movement and precision, as you seamlessly transition from angelic speedrunning to gunplay, dispatching demons with a variety of soul cards that double as weapons and parkour tools. The levels are meticulously designed, offering intricate pathways and multiple routes that reward mastery and exploration. The game's scoring system, which incentivizes fast completion times and stylish kills, further fuels the addictive nature of the gameplay, pushing you to constantly refine your skills and strive for perfection.

Neon White is a game that demands your attention and rewards your dedication. It's a game that will push you to your limits, but the satisfaction of mastering its challenges is truly unparalleled. If you're looking for an action game that will test your reflexes, ignite your competitive spirit, and leave you grinning from ear to ear, then Neon White is an absolute must-play.

Neon White has quickly become one of my all time favorites. Speed running done perfectly. It's more of a first person platformer than a shooter but does require some quick aim to get top times. You collect cards that can be used as guns or discarded for certain abilities like jumps, stomps, etc to help you beat stages as quickly as possible. Most stages can be beaten in about 30 seconds but you'll be playing it over and over and over to unlock the ace medals. There are also collectible gifts to find on each stage that are never that hard to figure out.

The story is pretty interesting although the dialogue can often times be pretty dumb. Admittedly, I never really watched anime so I don't know if this is just in line with standard anime stuff or not. I mostly laughed at some of the dumb dialogue myself. The aesthetic is awesome though as is the music.

The game is just a ton of fun. If you don't like the dialogue, fast forward through all of it and enjoy some top notch game play. It's 100% worth your time.

The movement feels amazing and the soundtrack slaps. Can't recommend it enough. Beat my time, nerds.
